CognitoJwt.description: Cognito-issued JWT access token. Send as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Use the Authorize button to set it for all authenticated operations.

SuccessEnvelope.description: Standard success envelope returned by all endpoints.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Standard error envelope returned by all endpoints.

PaginationEnvelope.description: Standard list/collection payload. Lives inside the SuccessEnvelope `data`. The item array key is the plural resource name (e.g. `users`, `executions`).

count.description: Number of items in this page.

nextKey.description: Opaque base64 pagination token; pass as `start_key` on the next request. Null when no more pages remain.

AnalysisQueueRequest.description: Request body to queue a workflow for processing. The body carries an entry point plus exactly one workflow-config block that determines the workflow type: `calculation` (NCA analysis), `data_cleaning`, `custom_calculations`, `custom_plots`, `custom_tables`, or `custom_reports`. The entry point is `fileId` for a fresh file-based run (analysis, data-cleaning) or `parentExecutionId` for a run that chains off a prior execution (e.g. custom_calculations, custom_plots, custom_tables, custom_reports). See the named examples for a full body per workflow type. Fields are intentionally open (additionalProperties) because the config blocks evolve independently of this envelope — and array items inside `data_cleaning.rules` / `custom_calculations.calculations` are self-describing by their `type`, so their exact keys are documented by example rather than a fixed schema.

fileId.description: Entry point for a file-based run: the id of a previously-uploaded input file (from the file upload response). Mutually exclusive with parentExecutionId.

parentExecutionId.description: Entry point for a chained run (custom_calculations, custom_plots, custom_tables, custom_reports): the execution this run builds on. Mutually exclusive with fileId.

name.description: A human-friendly name for this execution.

calculation.description: NCA analysis configuration. Present for an nca_workflow. See the AnalysisQueueRequest 'Analysis (NCA)' example for a full block.

designations.description: BLQ / missing / concentration-unit designations. Each entry is a { value } or { column } selector.

columns.description: Column mappings (time, uniqueId, concentration.observed/analyzed, sorting[], grouping[], customColumns[]).

dosing.description: Dose amount/unit/frequency/type, each a { value } or { column } selector.

data_cleaning.description: Data-cleaning configuration. Contains a `rules[]` array. Each rule is self-describing by its `type` (from the preset catalog of rule types); the keys it accepts, and the column names / values they reference, depend on the rule type and the user's input file. Documented by example rather than a fixed per-type schema. Present for a data_cleaning_workflow.

custom_calculations.description: Custom post-analysis calculations configuration. Contains a `calculations[]` array (and an optional `output` block, e.g. `sort`). Each calculation is self-describing by its `type` (e.g. `ratio`); the keys it accepts (numerator/denominator/conditions/paramcd/etc.) depend on the calculation type and reference the analysis result columns. Documented by example rather than a fixed per-type schema. Chains off a prior execution via `parentExecutionId`.

custom_plots.description: Custom plotting configuration. Contains a `plots[]` array. Each plot is self-describing by its `type` (e.g. `individual_linear`, `mean_semilog`); the axis/column/grouping/condition keys it accepts depend on the plot type and reference the analysis result columns. Documented by example rather than a fixed per-type schema. Chains off a prior execution via `parentExecutionId`; may be combined with `custom_tables` in one body.

custom_tables.description: Custom tables configuration. Contains a `tables[]` array. Each table is self-describing by its `type` (e.g. `individual_pk_parameters`, `summary_pk_parameters`); the columns/stats/groups/conditions/replacementMapping/layout keys it accepts depend on the table type and reference the analysis result columns. Documented by example rather than a fixed per-type schema. Chains off a prior execution via `parentExecutionId`; may be combined with `custom_plots` in one body.

metadata.description: Optional caller-defined metadata stored with the execution (e.g. project id, tags).

AuditLogEntry.description: An immutable audit log entry (21 CFR Part 11 style). Records who did what to which resource, with an optional change diff.

tenantId.description: Tenant that owns the affected resource.

Execution.description: An analysis execution summary. The same shape is returned by the status, root, history, and lineage endpoints (history/lineage return arrays of this). Fields are formatted by ExecutionSummaryFormatter.to_api_response.

input.description: The original analysis input (e.g. fileId, config references).

error.description: First error, if any (same element as errors[0]).

children.description: Populated only in tree/lineage views; child executions nested under a root.

ExecutionPhase.description: A single phase within an execution (e.g. nca_analysis, custom_calculations, custom_reports).

ExecutionStep.description: A single step within an execution phase.

FeatureFlagRule.description: A feature-flag rule enabling/disabling a feature key for a given scope.

featureKey.description: The registered feature key this rule targets.

scope.description: The scope level the rule applies to (e.g. global, tenant, user).

scopeId.description: Identifier within the scope (e.g. a tenant id or user id); null for global scope.

FeatureFlagRuleCreateRequest.description: Request body to create a feature-flag rule.

FeatureKeyRegisterRequest.description: Request body to register (or update) a feature key.

FeatureKeyRegistration.description: A registered feature key that rules can target.

File.description: File metadata record (the file's bytes live in S3; this is metadata + references).

PresignedUploadResponse.description: A presigned S3 upload target. POST the file to `url` with the given `fields` (S3 POST policy) or PUT to `url` depending on method.

fields.description: Form fields to include with an S3 POST upload.

key.description: S3 object key the upload targets.

QueueAcceptedResponse.description: Acknowledgement that an analysis was accepted onto the workflow queue. `status` is `queued` normally, or `throttled` when admission delayed it (with `delaySeconds`).

delaySeconds.description: Present only when status is throttled.

ReportTemplate.description: A custom report template owned by a tenant.

ownershipLevel.description: Ownership scope of the template (e.g. tenant, platform).

Subscription.description: A tenant subscription (billing plan + limits). Aplos-specific limits (executions, profiles, seats, storage) are stored under `metadata`.

metadata.description: Custom key/value store. Aplos platform limits live here.

Tenant.description: A customer organization (tenant) in the multi-tenant platform.

maxUsers.description: Maximum users allowed; null means unlimited.

TenantUpsertRequest.description: Request body to create or update a tenant. On create, name is required; on update (with a tenant id in the path), only provided fields change.

identityProvider.description: Primary identity provider: cognito | google | office365 | facebook | saml

UserUpsertRequest.description: Request body to create or update a user. On create, email is required; on update, only the provided fields are changed.

ValidationTriggerResponse.description: Acknowledgement that a validation workflow was queued.

BadRequest.description: Bad request — validation error or malformed input.
